questions.q: Which of the following is CORRECT with respect to the property mentioned against it?
options: Osmotic pressure at 298K : 0.1M NaCl solution < 0.1M Urea solution
Concentration of NaCl in the solution : 2ppm > 2M
Vapour pressure at 298K : Salt water < Pure water
questions.explanation: Dissolving a non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure (Raoult's law), so salt water has a lower vapour pressure than pure water; the other three statements are each reversed from the true relationship.

questions.q:
Match List - I (Laws) with the List - II (Mathematical expressions):
List - I: (a) Henry's law (b) Raoult's law (c) First law of thermodynamics (d) Kohlrausch's law
List - II: (i) $P_1 = x_1P_1^0$ (ii) $p = K_Hx$ (iii) $\Lambda_m^0 = \nu_+\lambda_+^0 + \nu_-\lambda_-^0$ (iv) $\Delta U = q + w$
Codes:
options: a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
a - ii, b - i, c - iii, d - iv
a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
a - i, b - ii, c - iv, d - iii
questions.explanation: Henry's law is $p=K_Hx$ (ii), Raoult's law is $P_1=x_1P_1^0$ (i), the first law is $\Delta U=q+w$ (iv), and Kohlrausch's law is $\Lambda_m^0=\nu_+\lambda_+^0+\nu_-\lambda_-^0$ (iii).

questions.q: When 0.0106 mole of acetic acid was dissolved in 1 kg of water, the freezing point depression for this strength of acid was 0.0205 K. If the calculated freezing point depression is 0.0197 K, Van't Hoff factor (i) and degree of dissociation of acetic acid respectively are
questions.explanation: $i = \Delta T_{f,observed}/\Delta T_{f,calculated} = 0.0205/0.0197 \approx 1.041$; for HA $\rightleftharpoons$ H$^+$+A$^-$, $i = 1+\alpha$, so $\alpha = 0.041$.

questions.q: The relative lowering of vapour pressure produced by dissolving 18 g of urea (Molar mass = 60 g mol$^{-1}$) in 100 g of water is
questions.explanation: Moles urea = 18/60 = 0.3; moles water = 100/18 $\approx$ 5.56; relative lowering of vapour pressure = mole fraction of solute = 0.3/(0.3+5.56) $\approx$ 0.05.

questions.q: Which of the following methods of expressing concentration are unitless?
questions.explanation: Mole fraction (ratio of moles) and mass percent (ratio of masses) are both dimensionless ratios, unlike molality (mol/kg) and molarity (mol/L) which carry units.

questions.q: Among the following 0.1 m aqueous solutions, which one will exhibit the lowest boiling point elevation, assuming complete ionization of the compounds in solution?
questions.explanation: Boiling point elevation is proportional to the van't Hoff factor i; NaCl gives i=2, the smallest among NaCl(2), AlCl$_3$(4), Al$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$(5) and K$_2$SO$_4$(3), so it shows the lowest elevation.

questions.q: Variation of solubility with temperature T for a gas in liquid is shown by the following graphs. The correct representation is [graphs of Solubility vs T: (1) an increasing straight line, (2) a constant/flat line, (3) a curve rising then falling (peak), (4) a decreasing straight line]
options: Solubility rises then falls with T
questions.explanation: The solubility of a gas in a liquid decreases with increasing temperature (dissolution of gases is exothermic), so the correct graph is a decreasing curve.

questions.q: 180g of glucose, C$_6$H$_{12}$O$_6$, is dissolved in 1 kg of water in a vessel. The temperature at which water boils at 1.013 bar is _____ (given, K$_b$ for water is 0.52 K kg mol$^{-1}$. Boiling point for pure water is 373.15 K)
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose = 180/180 = 1 mol, so molality = 1 mol/kg; $\Delta T_b = K_b m = 0.52\times1 = 0.52$ K, giving a boiling point of 373.15 + 0.52 = 373.67 K.

questions.q: If N$_2$ gas is bubbled through water at 293 K, how many moles of N$_2$ gas would dissolve in 1 litre of water? Assume that N$_2$ exerts a partial pressure of 0.987 bar. [Given K$_H$ for N$_2$ at 293 K is 76.48 K bar]
questions.explanation: By Henry's law, mole fraction x = p/K$_H$ = 0.987/76480 ≈ 1.29×10$^{-5}$; with 1 L water ≈ 55.5 mol, moles of N$_2$ ≈ x × 55.5 ≈ 7.16×10$^{-4}$ mol (option 4); KEA's revised key also accepted option 2 (0.716×10$^{-3}$ = 7.16×10$^{-4}$, the same value written differently).

questions.q: Vapour pressure of a solution containing 18 g of glucose and 178.2 g of water at 100°C is: (Vapour pressure of pure water at 100°C = 760 torr)
questions.explanation: n(water) = 9.9, n(glucose) = 0.1, mole fraction of glucose = 0.1/10 = 0.01; ($P_0-P_s$)/$P_0$ = 0.01 gives $P_s$ $\approx$ 752.0 torr.

questions.q: A mixture of phenol and aniline shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. This is due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: Phenol and aniline form an intermolecular hydrogen bond between -OH and -NH$_2$ groups, strengthening attractions and lowering the vapour pressure below the ideal value.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs will show positive deviation from Raoult's Law?
questions.explanation: Benzene disrupts the hydrogen-bonded structure of methanol without forming comparably strong new interactions, weakening intermolecular forces and giving a positive deviation.

questions.q: Dimerisation of solute molecules in low dielectric constant solvent is due to :
questions.explanation: In non-polar (low dielectric constant) solvents, solutes such as carboxylic acids associate into dimers through intermolecular hydrogen bonding, which shows up as an abnormally high molar mass.

questions.q: The swelling in feet and ankles of an aged person due to sitting continuously for long hours during travel, is reduced by soaking the feet in warm salt water. This is because of :
questions.explanation: The salt solution has a higher solute concentration than the swollen tissue fluid, so water moves out of the swollen cells into the surrounding salt water by osmosis, reducing the swelling.

questions.q: A sample of water is found to contain 5.85% $\left(\dfrac{w}{w}\right)$ of AB (molecular mass 58.5) and 9.50% $\left(\dfrac{w}{w}\right)$ XY$_2$ (molecular mass 95). Assuming 80% ionisation of AB and 60% ionisation of XY$_2$, the freezing point of water sample is [Given : K$_f$ for water 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$, Freezing point of pure water is 273 K and A, B and Y are monovalent ions)
questions.explanation: In 100 g of sample, AB gives 0.1 mol (van't Hoff factor i=1.8) and XY$_2$ gives 0.1 mol (i=2.2) dissolved in 84.65 g water; the total effective molality is about 4.73 m, so $\Delta T_f = K_f\times m_{eff} \approx 8.8\,K$, giving a freezing point of about 273 - 8.8 $\approx$ 264.25 K.

questions.q: An aqueous solution of alcohol contains 18 g of water and 414 g of ethyl alcohol. The mole fraction of water is
questions.explanation: Moles of water = 18/18 = 1; moles of ethanol = 414/46 = 9; mole fraction of water = 1/(1+9) = 0.1.

questions.q: Which of the following colligative properties can provide molar mass of proteins, polymers and colloids with greater precision?
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure produces a measurable effect even at very low concentrations, making it the preferred method for finding molar masses of macromolecules like proteins and polymers with greater precision.

questions.q: Solubility of a gas in a liquid increases with
options: increase of P and decrease of T
increase of P and increase of T
decrease of P and decrease of T
decrease of P and increase of T
questions.explanation: By Henry's law, gas solubility increases with increasing pressure; since dissolving a gas is exothermic, solubility also increases as temperature decreases.

questions.q: The rise in boiling point of a solution containing 1.8 g of glucose in 100 g of solvent is 0.1 °C. The molal elevation constant of the liquid is
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose = 1.8/180 = 0.01; molality = 0.01 mol / 0.1 kg = 0.1 m; K$_b$ = $\Delta$T$_b$/m = 0.1/0.1 = 1 K kg/mol.

questions.q: If 3 g of glucose (molar mass = 180 g) is dissolved in 60 g of water at 15 °C, the osmotic pressure of the solution will be
questions.explanation: Moles of glucose = 3/180 = 0.0167; taking the solution volume $\approx$ 60 mL = 0.06 L, C $\approx$ 0.278 mol/L; $\pi$ = CRT = 0.278 $\times$ 0.0821 $\times$ 288 $\approx$ 6.57 atm.

questions.q: Henry's law constant for the solubility of N$_2$ gas in water at 298 K is 1.0 × 10$^5$ atm. The mole fraction of N$_2$ in air is 0.8. The number of moles of N$_2$ from air dissolved in 10 moles of water at 298 K and 5 atm pressure is
questions.explanation: Partial pressure of N$_2$ = 0.8 × 5 = 4 atm. Mole fraction dissolved, x = p/K$_H$ = 4/10$^5$ = 4×10$^{-5}$. Moles of N$_2$ ≈ x × 10 (moles of water) = 4.0 × 10$^{-4}$.

questions.q: Choose the correct statement
options: K$_H$ value is same for a gas in any solvent
Higher the K$_H$ value more the solubility of gas
K$_H$ value increases on increasing the temperature of the solution
Easily liquefiable gases usually has lesser K$_H$ values
questions.explanation: Since solubility of a gas decreases with rise in temperature, the Henry's law constant K$_H$ increases with increase in temperature.

questions.q: The K$_H$ value (K bar) of Argon (I), Carbondioxide (II) formuldehyde (III) and methane (IV) are respectively 40.3, 1.67, 1.83 × 10$^{-5}$ and 0.413 at 298 K. The increasing order of solubility of gas in liquid is
questions.explanation: Solubility is inversely proportional to K$_H$. Decreasing K$_H$ order: I(40.3) > II(1.67) > IV(0.413) > III(1.83×10$^{-5}$), so increasing solubility order is I < II < IV < III.

questions.q: The vapour pressure of pure liquids A and B are 450 and 700 mm of Hg at 350 K respectively. If the total vapour pressure of the mixture is 600 mm of Hg, the composition of the solution in the mixture is
Which of the following pair of solutions is isotonic?
questions.explanation: Isotonic solutions need equal total particle concentration (i$\times$C): 0.01 M BaCl$_2$ (i=3) gives 0.03 M, and 0.015 M NaCl (i=2) also gives 0.03 M.

questions.q: Solute 'X' dimerises in water to the extent of 80%. 2.5g of 'X' in 100g of water increases the boiling point by 0.3°C. [K$_b$ = 0.52 K kg mol$^{-1}$] 'X' is molar mass is
questions.explanation: Van't Hoff factor $i = 1-\alpha+\alpha/2 = 1-0.8+0.4 = 0.6$. $\Delta T_b = iK_b\dfrac{w\times1000}{M\times W}$ gives $0.3 = 0.6\times0.52\times\dfrac{2.5\times1000}{M\times100}$, so $M = 26$.

questions.q: Relative lowering of vapour pressure of a dilute solution of glucose dissolved in 1 kg of water is 0.002. The molality of the solution is
questions.explanation: For a dilute solution, relative lowering of vapour pressure $\approx x_{solute} = n_{solute}/n_{solvent}$; with $n_{solvent}=1000/18=55.5$ mol, $n_{solute}=0.002\times55.5\approx0.111$ mol, giving molality $\approx0.111$ mol/kg.

questions.q: A non-volatile solute 'A' tetramerises in water to the extent of 80%. 2.5 g of 'A' in 100 g of water lowers the freezing point by 0.3 $^\circ$C. The molar mass of A in g mol$^{-1}$ is (K$_f$ for water = 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: Association into tetramers with 80% association gives van't Hoff factor $i=1-\alpha+\alpha/4=1-0.8+0.2=0.4$; molality $m=(2.5\times1000)/(M\times100)=25/M$; $\Delta T_f=iK_fm \Rightarrow 0.3=0.4\times1.86\times(25/M) \Rightarrow M=62$ g/mol.

questions.q: Solution 'A' contains acetone dissolved in chloroform and solution 'B' contains acetone dissolved in carbon disulphide. The type of deviations from Raoult's law shown by solutions A and B, respectively are
questions.explanation: Acetone-chloroform interactions (H-bonding) are stronger than the pure component interactions, causing negative deviation (solution A), while acetone-CS2 interactions are weaker, causing positive deviation (solution B).

questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solutions should have the highest boiling point ?
questions.explanation: Boiling point elevation depends on the total number of particles (van't Hoff factor i). Na$_2$SO$_4$ gives i=3 (2Na$^+$ + SO$_4^{2-}$), higher than the others (i=2), so it has the highest boiling point at equal molarity.

questions.q: Isotonic solutions are solutions having the same
questions.explanation: Isotonic solutions are, by definition, solutions that exert the same osmotic pressure at a given temperature.

questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solution has highest freezing point ?
questions.explanation: Freezing-point depression is proportional to $i \times m$; NH$_4$Cl gives the fewest ions ($i=2$) among the given 0.1 molal solutions, so it has the smallest depression and hence the highest freezing point.

questions.q: The Vant Hoff's factor 'i' accounts for
questions.explanation: The Van't Hoff factor i = (actual number of particles)/(number of formula units), which measures the extent of dissociation (or association) of the solute.

questions.q: When the pure solvent diffuses out of the solution through the semi-permeable membrane then the process is called
questions.explanation: Normal osmosis moves solvent into the solution; forcing solvent out of a solution through a semipermeable membrane (against the natural gradient) is reverse osmosis.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a colligative property ?
questions.explanation: Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles; optical activity is a property of molecular structure, not particle count.

questions.q: When an electrolyte is dissociated in solution, the van't Hoff's factor (i) is,
questions.explanation: Dissociation increases the number of particles in solution, so i = (observed colligative property)/(calculated) > 1.

questions.q: Osmotic pressure of the solution can be increased by,
options: increasing the temperature of the solution.
decreasing the temperature of the solution.
increasing the volume of the vessel.
questions.explanation: Since $\Pi = CRT$, osmotic pressure increases with increasing temperature at constant concentration.

questions.q: 0.06% (w/v) aqueous solution of urea is isotonic with
questions.explanation: 0.06 g urea (M=60) per 100 mL = 0.6 g/L / 60 g mol$^{-1}$ = 0.01 M; isotonic solutions have equal molar concentration, so the matching glucose solution is 0.01 M.

questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solution has the highest freezing point?
questions.explanation: Freezing point depression depends on effective particle concentration (i $\times$ C); 0.01 M NaCl gives the lowest effective concentration (0.02) among the options, so it has the smallest depression and hence the highest freezing point.

questions.q: After adding non-volatile solute freezing point of water decreases to $-$0.186 $^\circ$C. Calculate $\Delta T_b$ if K$_f$ = 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$ and K$_b$ = 0.521 K kg mol$^{-1}$
questions.explanation: $\Delta T_f$ = 0.186 K gives molality m = $\Delta T_f$/K$_f$ = 0.186/1.86 = 0.1; then $\Delta T_b$ = K$_b$ $\times$ m = 0.521 $\times$ 0.1 = 0.0521 K.

questions.q: 5.5 mg of nitrogen gas dissolves in 180 g of water at 273 K and one atm pressure due to nitrogen gas. The mole fraction of nitrogen in 180 g of water at 5 atm nitrogen pressure is approximately
questions.explanation: At 1 atm, moles N$_2$ = 5.5×10$^{-3}$/28 ≈ 1.96×10$^{-4}$, moles water = 180/18 = 10, so x(N$_2$) ≈ 1.96×10$^{-5}$; by Henry's law, at 5 atm the mole fraction is 5× this ≈ 1×10$^{-4}$.

questions.q: A solution of 1.25 g of 'P' in 50 g of water lowers freezing point by 0.3 °C. Molar mass of 'P' is 94. K$_{f(water)}$ = 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$. The degree of association of 'P' in water is
questions.explanation: Calculated ΔT$_f$ (i=1) = 1.86×1000×1.25/(94×50) = 0.495 °C; van't Hoff factor i = 0.3/0.495 = 0.606. For dimerisation, i = 1 - α/2, giving α ≈ 0.787 (≈79%), closest to 80%. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: For an ideal binary liquid mixture
questions.explanation: For an ideal binary liquid mixture, ΔH$_{mix}$ = 0 and ΔV$_{mix}$ = 0, while mixing is spontaneous so ΔS$_{mix}$ > 0 and ΔG$_{mix}$ < 0.

questions.q: Which of the following is 'NOT' a colligative property ?
questions.explanation: All four listed properties are actually colligative properties, so the question has no valid 'NOT' answer; KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates.

questions.q: 3 gms of urea is dissolved in 45 gms of H$_2$O. The relative lowering in vapour pressure is
questions.explanation: Moles urea = 3/60 = 0.05; moles water = 45/18 = 2.5; relative lowering $\approx$ n(solute)/n(solvent) = 0.05/2.5 = 0.02.

questions.q: Which of the following aqueous solutions will exhibit highest boiling point ?
questions.explanation: Effective particle concentration (i $\times$ C) is highest for 0.01 M Na$_2$SO$_4$ (i=3, giving 0.03), producing the greatest boiling point elevation.

questions.q: The mass of a non-volatile solute of molar mass 40 g mol$^{-1}$ that should be dissolved in 114 g of octane to lower its vapour pressure by 20% is
questions.explanation: By Raoult's law, $\dfrac{\Delta P}{P} = x_{solute}=0.2$. Moles of octane (M=114) = 1, so $n/(n+1)=0.2 \Rightarrow n=0.25$ mol, mass $=0.25\times40=10$ g.

questions.q: The vapour pressures of two liquids A and B in their pure states are in the ratio of 1 : 2. A binary solution of A and B contains A and B in the mole proportion of 1 : 2. The mole fraction of A in the vapour phase of the solution will be
questions.explanation: Take $P_A^\circ=p, P_B^\circ=2p$, $x_A=1/3, x_B=2/3$. Partial pressures: $P_A=p/3, P_B=4p/3$. Mole fraction of A in vapour $=\dfrac{p/3}{p/3+4p/3}=\dfrac{1}{5}=0.2$.

questions.q: The empirical formula of a nonelectrolyte is $CH_2O$. A solution containing 3 g of the compound exerts the same osmotic pressure as that of 0.05 M glucose solution. The molecular formula of the compound is..................
questions.explanation: Equal osmotic pressure implies equal molarity (0.05 M); molar mass = 3 g / 0.05 mol = 60 g/mol = 2×(empirical formula mass 30), giving the molecular formula $C_2H_4O_2$.

questions.q: A solution of two liquids boils at a temperature more than the boiling point of either of them. Hence, the binary solution shows ..............
options: positive or negative deviation from Raoult's law depending upon the composition
questions.explanation: A solution boiling higher than either pure component has a lower vapour pressure than expected from stronger unlike-molecule interactions, which is a negative deviation from Raoult's law.

questions.q: The empirical formula of a nonelectrolyte is $C_1H_2O_1$. A solution containing 6 g of the compound exerts the same osmotic pressure as that of 0.05 M glucose solution at the same temperature. The molecular formula of the compound is ...............
questions.explanation: Equal osmotic pressure at the same temperature means equal molar concentration (0.05 M); for 6 g in 1 L this gives a molar mass of 120 g/mol, i.e. $(CH_2O)_4 = C_4H_8O_4$.

questions.q: Vapour pressure of pure 'A' is 70 mm of Hg at 25 °C. It forms an ideal solution with 'B' in which mole fraction of A is 0.8. If the vapour pressure of the solution is 84 mm of Hg at 25 °C, the vapour pressure of pure 'B' at 25 °C is
questions.explanation: By Raoult's law, $84 = 70(0.8) + P_B^0(0.2) = 56 + 0.2P_B^0 \Rightarrow P_B^0 = 140$ mm.

questions.q: A 6% solution of urea is isotonic with
questions.explanation: 6% urea (M=60) = 60 g/L = 1 M; isotonic solutions of non-electrolytes have equal molar concentration, i.e. 1 M glucose.

questions.q: In countries nearer to polar region, the roads are sprinkled with CaCl$_2$. This is
options: to minimise the accumulation of dust on the road
to minimise the wear and tear of the roads
questions.explanation: CaCl$_2$ actually works by depressing the freezing point of ice/snow (a colligative effect) so it melts faster; none of the listed options state this correctly, which is why KEA awarded a grace mark.

questions.q: Cooking is fast in a pressure cooker, because
options: food is cooked at constant volume.
loss of heat due to radiation is minimum.
water boils at higher temperature inside the pressure cooker.
questions.explanation: Increased pressure inside the sealed cooker raises the boiling point of water, so cooking occurs at a higher temperature, speeding up cooking.
